youtube_title: The Pentagon Reportedly Wants Bases Ready for 90 Days. Could Your House Last 3?
youtube:
The Pentagon's FORTRESS America plan starts with military bases making their own power, and Fox News reports, citing documents it reviewed, that major bases would be expected to run at least 90 days on their own. It's not a blackout notice: nothing announced schedules power cuts for homes. Your first hour of an outage: flashlights, not candles. Unplug electronics. Keep the fridge and freezer shut. Report it to your power company (NIPSCO: text OUT to 444111). Stay away from downed power lines. Check on neighbors if it's safe. Part 1 of 3. #PowerOutage #BePrepared #WinterReady #LaPorte #Indiana

youtube_title: Power Out in Winter? How to Stay Warm Safely | Could Your House Last 3 Days? Part 2
youtube:
Part 2: staying warm when the power's out. A generator goes outside only, at least 20 feet from windows, doors and vents, and never in the garage, even with the door open. Never plug it into a wall outlet. Your carbon monoxide alarm needs batteries or battery backup. Never heat with a gas oven, stove or grill. Headache, dizziness, weakness, upset stomach, vomiting, chest pain, confusion, or an alarm going off? Get outside, then call 911. Layer up and close off rooms you don't need. Can't keep warm? Go somewhere with heat; in Indiana, call 2-1-1 to find a warming center. Part 2 of 3. #WinterReady #PowerOutage #CarbonMonoxide #LaPorte #Indiana

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission; CDC; Ready.gov (FEMA); National Weather Service; Indiana Department of Homeland Security; Minnesota State Fire Marshal; Indiana FSSA (Indiana 211).

youtube_title: Power Out? The 4-Hour Fridge Rule and the Water You Need | Could Your House Last 3 Days? Part 3
youtube:
Part 3: food and water. With the doors shut, a fridge keeps food cold about 4 hours and a full freezer about 48 (24 if half full). Keep the fridge at 40°F or colder and the freezer at 0°F. Fridge without power more than 4 hours? Toss perishables like meat, milk, eggs and leftovers, and never taste-test: when in doubt, throw it out. Store at least 1 gallon of water per person, per day, for at least 3 days (2 weeks at home if you can), and ask your pharmacist now about medicine that needs the fridge. Scoop's 90-Day Grid-Down Survival Guide is on the ScoopAndDude Etsy shop. Part 3 of 3. #PowerOutage #FoodSafety #BePrepared #LaPorte #Indiana
